speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER I. THERE IS NO ONE LEFT. When Mary Lennox was sent to live with her uncle at Misselthwaite Manor, everyone described her as the most unpleasant-looking child they had ever seen. And it was true. She had a thin face, a frail body, limp yellow hair, and a constant scowl. Her hair and skin were a pale, sickly yellow because she had been born in India and had spent her childhood suffering from one illness after another. Her father held a post in the British government and was always busy and sick himself. Her mother, a famous beauty, cared only for parties and socializing. She had never wanted a little girl, so when Mary was born, she immediately handed her over to a native nanny, or Ayah. The nanny was instructed to keep the child out of sight to avoid disturbing the mother. So, as a sickly, crying, unattractive baby, Mary was kept hidden away. As she grew into a frail, irritable toddler, she remained hidden.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mary only remembered seeing the faces of her nanny and the other local servants. Because her mother would be furious if the child's crying disturbed her, the servants always obeyed Mary and let her have her way in everything. By the time she was six years old, she had become as spoiled and selfish as a child could possibly be. Her first young English governess, hired to teach her to read and write, disliked her so much that she quit within three months. Other teachers came and went even faster. If Mary hadn't decided on her own that she wanted to read books, she would never have learned the alphabet at all.

speaker: Narrator
text: One brutally hot morning, when she was about nine years old, she woke up feeling extremely irritable. She grew even angrier when she saw a strange servant standing by her bed instead of her usual nanny.

speaker: Mary
text: Why are you here? Get out! Send my nanny to me.

speaker: Narrator
text: The woman looked terrified but could only stammer that

speaker: Servant
text: the nanny could not come.

speaker: Narrator
text: When Mary flew into a rage, kicking and hitting her, the woman grew even more frightened, repeating that

speaker: Servant
text: it was simply impossible for the nanny to come.

speaker: Narrator
text: Something strange was in the air that morning. The household routine was broken, and several of the servants had disappeared. The ones Mary did see moved silently and hurried past with pale, terrified faces. No one would explain what was happening, and her nanny still did not appear. As the morning went on, Mary was completely left to herself. Eventually, she wandered out into the garden and began playing alone under a tree near the porch. She pretended to plant a flower bed, sticking bright red hibiscus blossoms into little mounds of dirt. All the while, her anger grew. She muttered to herself, planning the insults she would scream at her nanny, Saidie, once she returned.

speaker: Mary
text: Pig! Pig! Daughter of pigs!

speaker: Narrator
text: she whispered, using the worst insult she knew. She was grinding her teeth and repeating this when she heard her mother walk onto the porch with a guest. She was with a young, fair-skinned officer who looked like a boy, whom Mary knew had recently arrived from England. The child stared at them, focusing especially on her mother. Mary rarely got to see her, and she was always mesmerized by how tall, slim, and beautiful her mother was, always dressed in lovely clothes. Her mother had silky, curly hair, a delicate nose, and large, bright eyes that usually seemed to be laughing. She wore light, flowing dresses that Mary described as being full of lace. This morning, her dresses seemed even more elegant, but her eyes were wide with fear as she looked up at the young officer.

speaker: Mother
text: Is it really that bad? Oh, is it?

speaker: Narrator
text: Mary heard her ask.

speaker: Officer
text: It's terrible. Terrible, Mrs. Lennox. You should have left for the cooler mountain regions weeks ago.

speaker: Narrator
text: Her mother wrung her hands.

speaker: Mother
text: Oh, I know I should have! I only stayed behind for that silly dinner party. What a fool I was!

speaker: Narrator
text: Just then, a loud, piercing wail erupted from the servants' quarters. Her mother clutched the young officer's arm, and Mary began to shiver from head to toe. The crying grew louder and more frantic.

speaker: Mother
text: What is that? What is happening?

speaker: Narrator
text: Mrs. Lennox gasped.

speaker: Officer
text: Someone has died. You didn't tell me that it had reached your servants.

speaker: Mother
text: I didn't know! Come with me! Come inside!

speaker: Narrator
text: She turned and ran back into the house. After that, horrifying things happened, and the mystery of the morning was finally explained. Cholera had broken out in its most deadly form, and people were dying rapidly. Mary's nanny had fallen ill during the night, and her sudden death was the reason for the servants' crying. Before the next day, three more servants died, and the rest fled in terror.
